objective: Prove mechanical truth, visual comparison and direct-response usefulness on the most claim-sensitive topic: a puncture is repairable only in the tread area, under 1/4 inch, with a plug plus an inside patch.
mechanicTruth: A puncture in the tread area is often repairable. A proper repair means taking the tire off the wheel, inspecting it inside, and filling the hole with a plug (stem) plus sealing it with an inside patch. Punctures in the sidewall or shoulder, or larger than 1/4 inch, are not repairable; the tire is replaced.
loopIdea: The last beat returns to the nail in the tread from the hook, now with the zone outline around it, so the loop restarts on the question the Reel answers.
selectedCaption: Nail in the tire: patch or replace? It depends on where and how big. In the tread area and under a quarter inch, it is often repairable — tire off the wheel, inspected inside, plug plus an inside patch. In the sidewall or shoulder, or bigger than a quarter inch, the tire is replaced. Stop by Nick's Tire & Auto, Euclid Ave, Cleveland.
voiceoverScript: Nail in the tire: patch or replace? In the tread area and under a quarter inch, it is often repairable. A proper repair comes off the wheel, gets inspected inside, then a plug plus an inside patch. Sidewall or shoulder, or over a quarter inch: replace. Bring the tire; we look inside first.
